CausalChain: IDH mutation in iCCA -> 2-HG accumulation -> Inhibition of DNA/histone demethylases -> Selective epigenetic upregulation of cytokine gene promoters -> Increased secretion of fibroblast-activating cytokines (e.g., TGF-β, IL-6) -> Recruitment/activation of CAFs -> ECM remodeling and enhanced chemoresistance
Hypothesis: In IDH-mutant intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma, 2-hydroxyglutarate induced epigenetic alterations drive the overexpression of fibroblast-activating cytokines, which in turn reprogram the tumor microenvironment by augmenting CAF recruitment and activation. This CAF-driven remodeling fosters chemoresistance; therefore, targeting the epigenetic machinery that regulates cytokine production may disrupt this supportive stroma and enhance treatment efficacy.
Abstract: Intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma (iCCA) frequently harbors IDH mutations, which lead to the accumulation of the oncometabolite 2-hydroxyglutarate (2-HG). We hypothesize that this epigenetic reprogramming drives a selective upregulation of cytokine genes, notably those encoding fibroblast-activating factors. The resulting heightened secretion of cytokines, such as TGF-β and IL-6, promotes the recruitment and activation of cancer‐associated fibroblasts (CAFs) within the tumor microenvironment. CAFs in turn remodel the extracellular matrix and contribute to chemoresistance. Targeting the downstream epigenetic mediators responsible for cytokine upregulation may thus disrupt the tumor-stroma cross-talk and improve therapeutic outcomes. This concept provides a novel angle for potential intervention in a subset of iCCA patients with IDH mutations.
